title: Hometown Heros help improve animal welfare - NewsBreak
text:
By Gabriella Winans ,
57 minutes ago YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio (WYTV) — This week’s Hometown Hero goes to a local nonprofit with a goal to improve animal welfare.
The Mahoning County Animal Advocates started their nonprofit in February 2025 with a mission of helping emaciated companion pets. Since then, they’ve been able to donate almost 12,000 pounds of dog and cat food.
Jan Nelson and Drea Lewinksy-Riebe serve as president and vice president of the nonprofit.
“We started because we love animals, and along the way we realized it’s really about helping people who love their pets,” Nelson said.
Each month, they donate 1,000 pounds of dog and cat food to the Youngstown Community Food Center and 200 pounds to the Veterans’ Outreach.
Their belief is that if they help the people, then they help the pets.
“People are really struggling, and we don’t want them to have to decide between feeding themselves or feeding their pets, or even making that terrible decision to have to give their pet up and surrender their pet because they can’t feed it,” Nelson said.
All of it is done through donations and fundraisers. The advocates organize everything out of their homes to help their cause.
“We wanted to not flood our local agencies. We just saw the need and how they’re so flooded. People are in dire situations. We figured if we can do this, then we can help the other agencies as well,” Lewinsky-Riebe said.
The Mahoning County Animal Advocates are currently accepting pet food donations. They say the most rewarding part is knowing they are helping both people and their pets.
“We’ve realized it’s really about helping people, because they love their pets. We don’t want them to have to make a decision between keeping them or not,” Nelson said.
